sources.title: How much has UK fiscal headroom narrowed ahead of autumn budget? (Investing.com, citing UBS)
sources.notes: Press coverage used only as qualitative context: UBS estimated gilt yields about 70 basis points above the March assumption, removing roughly £10bn of headroom; the Budget is on 28 October 2026.

sources.title: Direct effects of illustrative tax changes bulletin (June 2025)
sources.notes: Methodology notes: direct effects on the tax base and closely related bases; behavioural responses via taxable income elasticities and tax-motivated incorporation; wider economic effects excluded; rate changes scale roughly linearly, allowances and limits do not; CGT and SDLT non-linear and asymmetrical.

sources.title: Compliance review of the Direct effects of illustrative tax changes bulletin (Office for Statistics Regulation)
sources.notes: December 2025 review prompted by concerns about transparency of pre- and post-behavioural estimates; recommends a detailed methodology document and reconsideration of the official statistics label.

sources.title: Schedule of updates and announcements for HMRC's statistics
sources.notes: 6 July 2026 entry: publication of the Direct effects of illustrative tax changes bulletin (due 7 July 2026) deferred to complete a review of the key assumptions underpinning some of the estimates.

sources.title: Statement of Funding Policy: Funding the Scottish Government, Welsh Government and Northern Ireland Executive
sources.notes: Barnett formula (paragraphs 3.9-3.18): change to planned UK Government departmental spending × comparability factor × population proportion, applied to resource and capital DEL separately. Annex B lists the departmental comparability factors used at Spending Review 2025; the FCDO and Ministry of Defence undertake only reserved activities and have none (B.12).
